items.summary: The `design` enforcement_level is overloaded: in ckeletin-rust's report it labels both structurally-strong enforcement (CKSPEC-ARCH-007 — a stray root .rs file belongs to no crate and is not built, effectively compile-time) and near-attestation (CKSPEC-CL-004, ENF-003, ENF-004 — 'documented in the CONFORMANCE.md audit table'). One label thus spans the strongest and weakest ends of the ladder and no longer communicates enforcement strength. Surfaced when enforcement_level validation was first added (it was previously unvalidated, so `design`/`test` shipped unchecked). Independently re-confirmed 2026-06-25 by the a0 dogfooding review (its finding #4): the ENF-002 ladder (compile-time, linter, SAST, script, CI, honor-system) and the schema's added `test`/`design` levels disagree, and `design` admittedly spans compile-time-strong to honor-system-weak.
items.rationale: Proposed resolution to discuss with the consumer: introduce a distinct `structural` level for the un-buildable cases and route documentation/attestation cases to `honor-system`, then have ckeletin-rust reclassify its 6 `design` entries. Held at `discuss` rather than `update` because the conformance/*.yaml aggregates are regenerated from ckeletin-rust's published data, so the implementation gets a vote before the enum changes; adding `structural` to the schema before any consumer uses it would be decorative vocabulary.

items.summary: The spec defines language implementations and 'CLI application scaffolds' but never defines the consumer/export boundary: which artifacts are reference-implementation truth versus derived-project truth. Exposed scaffolding a0 from ckeletin-rust — the clone dragged ckeletin-rust's OWN root-level conformance/prose artifacts (CONFORMANCE.md, conformance-mapping.toml, conformance-report.json, conformance/requirements.json, spec-feedback/planning docs) into the consumer, where they read as authoritative about a0 even though `just conform` is upstream-only there. NB: this is the scaffold/init export path, NOT `just ckeletin-update` (which only propagates `.ckeletin/`). A concrete sub-instance: a framework-owned recipe (`.ckeletin/Justfile` ckeletin-fuzz) hardcodes a consumer-owned filename (`--test fuzz_ping`), so a consumer that replaces `ping` carries a stale target. Cuts against P7 (SSOT) and P9 (Automated Enforcement). Refs: README.md:8, README.md:104, spec/05-agent-readiness.yaml:20, spec/02-enforcement.yaml:242.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss before writing a requirement): add a scaffold-projection/export requirement that makes every artifact classify as framework-owned, consumer-owned, generated-evidence, or upstream-only; `init` MUST reset/remove/mark upstream-only conformance+prose evidence so a derived project never presents inherited reference-impl truth as its own. Held at `discuss` because it is a new MUST that ckeletin-rust (and ckeletin-go) must be able to satisfy in `init`/scaffold before the spec mandates it — the implementations get a vote on the classification scheme and on what `init` does with upstream-only files.

items.summary: ARCH-001 mandates four layers (Entry, Command, Business Logic, Infrastructure) and ARCH-002/004/005 assume that shape, but real consumers need honest deviations the spec has not caught up to — e.g. ckeletin-rust already learned a consumer may legitimately declare infrastructure = [] (no shared-services layer). Written as universal, the four-layer rule forces consumers either to fake a layer or to look non-conformant when they are honestly simpler/different. Refs: spec/01-architecture.yaml:19, spec/01-architecture.yaml:40, spec/01-architecture.yaml:82.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss): either scope the four-layer MUST to reference scaffolds explicitly, or define the set of allowed consumer projections (which layers may be empty/absent) and how a projected layout reports conformance. Held at `discuss` because narrowing a long-standing MUST changes what every implementation's arch-allowlist test asserts; ckeletin-rust and ckeletin-go must agree on the projection model first.

items.summary: ENF-009 requires releases to verify conformance against the latest spec but does not distinguish 'implementation conformance' from 'consumer scaffold health'. A derived repo that inherits a release workflow where `just conform` no-ops can look ENF-009-compliant while proving nothing — a green no-op satisfying the gate by accident. Refs: spec/02-enforcement.yaml:242.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss): require the conformance gate to declare its subject — ckeletin implementation conformance, generated-project conformance, or project health — and state that a no-op gate MUST NOT count as ENF-009 satisfaction. Pairs with FB-002 (a consumer is not necessarily a ckeletin implementation). Held at `discuss` because it likely needs a 'consumer conformance mode' concept that the implementations must define and emit before the spec can require the gate to name its subject.

items.summary: OUT-002 says 'every command' MUST emit structured stdout in machine-readable mode but is silent on argument-parser/usage failures, which a CLI framework (clap, Cobra, Click) emits BEFORE a command resolves. ckeletin-rust documents clap usage errors as an exception that bypasses the JSON envelope; the spec should own that boundary rather than leave each implementation to decide. Refs: spec/04-output.yaml:40.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss): define the phase boundary explicitly — either parse errors MAY follow CLI-framework convention (machine-readable mode begins after argument parsing), or parse errors MUST be wrapped in the envelope too. Pick one and state it. Held at `discuss` because wrapping parser errors is a non-trivial implementation change (clap/Cobra emit before the handler runs); the implementations get a vote on feasibility before OUT-002 picks the stricter option.

items.summary: Spec rationales cited stale principle numbers from an earlier renumbering: Automated Enforcement as 2 (now 9), Separation of Concerns as 5 (now 8), Platforms/Not Features as 4 (now 5), Lean Iteration as 3 (now 4), Single Source of Truth as 9 (now 7), plus an orphan 'Framework Independence (Principle 6)' that principles.md no longer defines and two bare '(Principle 4)' citations. `task check` did not catch rationale drift. principles.md is the SSOT for the name<->number map. Refs: principles.md:70, principles.md:88, spec/01-architecture.yaml:48, spec/06-changelog.yaml:28.
items.rationale: Fixed 2026-06-25: corrected all 28 drifted citations across 01-architecture / 02-enforcement / 03-testing / 06-changelog (26 number-only via an SSOT-driven fixer; 'Framework Independence (Principle 6)' remapped to 'Separation of Concerns (Principle 8)' since its rationale text is verbatim the current SoC definition; two bare '(Principle 4)' reworded to name 'Platforms, Not Features (Principle 5)'). Added a permanent guard: scripts/validate_spec.py:validate_principle_citations() parses principles.md and asserts every '<Name> (Principle N)' citation in spec prose matches the canonical number — wired into `task check` and covered by tests/test_validate_spec.py::TestPrincipleCitations (incl. a real-spec regression guard). This makes the SSOT mechanically enforced (P9), not just asserted. No requirement IDs, levels, or conformance entries changed, so all consumers still conform; chose `update`/`done` rather than `discuss` because prose-citation accuracy needs no implementation vote.

items.summary: Several `checkable: true` requirements (e.g. AGENT-001/004, CL-002/006, ENF-003/004) carry semantic-sufficiency claims that grep/file-existence cannot fully verify; the reports honestly fall back to honor-system/design evidence, but the boolean `checkable` overstates what is machine-verifiable. Refs: spec/_schema.yaml:58, spec/05-agent-readiness.yaml:69, spec/06-changelog.yaml:40.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss): split `checkable` into structurally_checkable / semantically_reviewed / partially_checkable (or equivalent), so the field tells the truth about how much of a requirement a machine can confirm. Held at `discuss` because it is a schema change touching every requirement's metadata and both implementations' report generators; needs an agreed taxonomy before migration.

items.summary: Terminology tension: the README frames conformance reports as 'retrospectives, not audits', while ENF-004 requires a living enforcement 'audit table'. Adversarially this reads as the spec distancing itself from audits while mandating one. Low severity / likely rhetorical. Refs: README.md:12, spec/02-enforcement.yaml:80.
items.rationale: Proposed (to discuss): clarify the README wording, e.g. 'not punitive audits; they are evidence retrospectives backed by an enforcement audit table', so 'audit' has one consistent meaning. Held at `discuss` only to batch it with the other wording decisions; trivial to apply once the framing is agreed.
